tools/replay_lean_axiom_census.py: Complete 198-line owner reviewed. Extracts named axiom report rows, rejects duplicates/empty individual lists, optionally checks exact three numeric headers, renders explicit Census and compares fresh Lean stdout list to those supplied expectations. It does not discover all theorem declarations, enforce its declared AXIOM_WHITELIST, require nonempty expected rows or require count headers. A self-consistent empty/partial named report can pass its check route; current 86-row report is nonempty. Replay invokes lake build then Lean, not executed here.
tools/replay_full_axiom_census.py: Complete 95-line owner reviewed. Recursively discovers package-local modules, rejects absent/invalid names, enumerates all owner-module environment declarations, rejects duplicate/empty parsed output and unapproved axioms, then writes a newly dated receipt. Unlike named replay it requires nonempty census and enforces whitelist. It assumes previously built imports and does not bind output to source hashes/toolchain or run lake build itself. It mutates FullCensus and full_axiom_report, so not executed on preserved source.
code/deposit_paths.py: Complete 112-line custody helper reviewed. POSIX lexical canonicality, Windows reserved-name/ADS/control/trailing-dot guards, symlink/junction ancestry refusal, resolved containment, regular-file checks, casefold uniqueness and parsed hash manifests provide useful bounded path/census protections. Directory/extension/name exclusions are explicit. TOCTOU is not removed by prior path checks and caller-selected root is not authenticated. No filesystem mutation performed.
verify_deposit.py: Complete 226-line verifier reviewed. Two-way selected-file census, byte digests and required package structures are distinct from optional named pytest and Lean stages. No test runs by default despite Optional/Default header. Lean stage accepts absence of Census/Core after build and does not require any axiom output or expected declaration coverage, so a build exit code alone can produce proofs-and-census-verified wording. It does not authenticate bytes, test archived historical identity, or prove native host correctness. No subprocess stage executed.
scripts/build_deposit_zip.py: Complete 107-line builder reviewed. Uses the supplied manifest, validates initial source hashes/casefold uniqueness, fixes date from output filename and Unix regular-file metadata, then writes sorted members plus SHA256SUMS. The later read is not hash-rechecked, so concurrent edits between validation and write remain possible; output is overwritten directly, unlike atomic temporary archive in rebuild_release. Parent output ancestors are not validated by safe_path. Not run and historical ZIP preserved.
scripts/regen_sha256sums.py: Complete 99-line manifest tool reviewed. Shared path walker supplies explicit file selection, sorted raw-byte digests, first manifest then enclosing sums. --check is read-only; default overwrites both controls and does not authenticate or mathematically certify them. Separate files are not updated atomically. CRLF/LF differences must be reported as custody differences rather than semantic corruption. Not run.
tools/rebuild_release.py: Complete 339-line release tool reviewed. Default refresh scans current tree when deposit_paths exists, rewrites manifests, creates today's ZIP and deletes older dated ZIP; this contradicts the docstring's fixed-set-only description and would destroy the intentionally retained historical release if used naively. --check compares current manifests against old archive and therefore reports intended historical/current drift, not automatically a bad historical deposit. ZIP construction rechecks source hashes and replaces a temporary ZIP, but the two manifests are not a single atomic commit. Validation has a weaker independent path guard than deposit_paths. No refresh/check subprocess was run.
